passage: Dilnaz caught herself rolling her eyes again as Kashish took a long time to finish her slide in Tuesday's meeting. Dilnaz was tense: she and Rehana were both up for the same senior post, and she kept a private tally of every win Rehana had. That night she saw that the eye-roll had more to do with her own stress and pride than with Kashish. Next day she offered to sit with her for twenty minutes over the spreadsheet and agreed a clear time for handing over. She also stayed late on her own launch report, so the results showed on the dashboard. On Thursday Dilnaz's father was taken to hospital in the middle of launch week. She rang the office from the corridor, shaking. Kashish took her deck to the client call and finished the tests without being asked. Rehana, to Dilnaz's surprise, forwarded her own notes. Dilnaz had noticed a typo in Rehana's section of the shared draft and had been tempted to leave it for the boss to find, but she told Rehana directly instead. A week later Dilnaz brought Kashish coffee, thanked her in front of the team, and covered her when Kashish went to an appointment.

qa.q: Where was Dilnaz's father taken on Thursday?
How did Dilnaz's view of Kashish change, and what did Kashish's help show about working together?
qa.a: Dilnaz first rolled her eyes because Kashish was slow, then saw the contempt came from her own stress and pride and offered help with clear timing; later Kashish covered for her in an emergency, showing that mutual help matters more than any single task.

qa.q: What was Dilnaz feeling when she rang the office from the corridor?
qa.a: She felt frightened and overwhelmed, since she was shaking with her father in hospital during launch week.

qa.q: How could Dilnaz keep the rivalry with Rehana healthy?
qa.a: She could keep focusing on her own visible results, stay honest and never sabotage Rehana, letting the rivalry sharpen her work.

grounding: A young professional's rivalry for a promotion, contempt for a slower colleague and gratitude for emergency cover show three different workplace stances.
